extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry / commutative algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, properties, and exercises about support, associated primes/points, embedded primes, rational functions, coherence, and basic facts about morphisms of ringed spaces (from a textbook chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nilpotent elements detected by associated points
rubrics_metrics.description: An element of A is nilpotent if and only if it vanishes at every associated point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to relate nilradical/reducedness to associated points; Exercise 6.6.N relates the reduced locus to support of the nilradical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonreduced locus is closure of associated points subset
rubrics_metrics.description: The locus of points [p] of Spec A where the stalk A_p is nonreduced is the closure of some subset of the associated points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies where nonreduced behavior occurs in terms of associated points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedded point definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An associated point that is in the closure of another associated point is said to be an embedded point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, embedded primes are associated primes that are not generic points of irreducible components; see geometric incarnation (6.6.32).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced rings have no embedded primes
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is reduced, then Spec A has no embedded points/primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.6.R gives a proof showing embedded primes would force nilpotents; note converse is false (Remark 6.6.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements determined by localization at associated points
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of M (and sections of the corresponding sheaf) are determined by their localizations/germs at the associated points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is formalized via injectivity of the natural map M -> product_{p in Ass M} M_p (Exercise 6.6.I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of an element equals V(annihilator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supp m = V(Ann_A m) for an element m in an A-module M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.6.A (easy important exercise). The annihilator Ann_A m := {a in A : am = 0}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of support of a module
rubrics_metrics.description: Supp M := {p in Spec A : M_p ≠ 0}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a principal module Am generated by m, Supp M = Supp m = V(Ann m). If M is finitely generated over Noetherian A, Supp M is closed (Exercise 6.6.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support behaves in short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 is exact then Supp M = Supp M' ∪ Supp M''.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exercise 6.6.B. Warning that Supp M need not be closed in general (counterexample with A = Z and suitable M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes: definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The associated prime ideals of an A-module M are prime ideals of the form Ann_A(m) for some m in M; associated points are the corresponding points of Spec A; denote Ass_A M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology: 'associated points' and 'associated primes' used interchangeably. (Remarkary: some colloquially call them 'assassins'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes of a ring
rubrics_metrics.description: The associated primes of a ring A are Ass_A(A), i.e., associated primes when A is considered as an A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases: for an integral domain A, Ass A = {(0)} (Exercise 6.6.E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes of hypersurfaces in polynomial rings
rubrics_metrics.description: For k[x1,...,xn]/(f), the associated primes are the principal ideals generated by the prime factors of f (for UFD A this generalizes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.6.F; shows hypersurfaces (over UFD) have no embedded points coming from repeated non-prime factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization via injections A/p -> M
rubrics_metrics.description: A prime p is in Ass_A(M) iff there is an injection A/p -> M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.6.G drives home this characterization; useful for constructing associated primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ass M subset Supp M and equality in Noetherian case
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated then Supp M is closed and Ass M ⊂ Supp M; moreover, if A is Noetherian and M finitely generated then Supp M = Ass M (Proposition 6.6.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine Exercise 6.6.G(b) and Exercise 6.6.M to get equality under Noetherian hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonzero modules over Noetherian rings have associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a nonzero module over a Noetherian ring A then Ass_A M is nonempty; for any nonzero m in M there is an associated prime p containing Ann m and p = Ann(xm) for some x in A (Proposition 6.6.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Built from maximality/stabilization arguments (Exercise 6.6.H and Proposition 6.6.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural injection to localizations at associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: For M a module over Noetherian A, the natural map M -> ∏_{p in Ass M} M_p is injective (Exercise 6.6.I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In fact one needs only the maximal associated primes in the product; proof uses associated prime of kernel if nonzero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zerodivisors are union of associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: For A Noetherian and M an A-module, f is a zerodivisor on M iff f vanishes at an associated point of M; equivalently, the set of zerodivisors is the union of the associated prime ideals (Proposition 6.6.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses choosing m with Ann m = p; conversely use localization and injectivity of multiplication on localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of Ass in short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0, we have Ass M' ⊂ Ass M ⊂ Ass M' ∪ Ass M'' (Proposition 6.6.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First inclusion via submodule argument; second inclusion constructed by analyzing the submodule generated by element with given annihilator. Equality need not hold in general (cautionary counterexample 6.6.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness of associated primes for finitely generated modules over Noetherian rings
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated over a Noetherian ring A then M has a finite filtration 0 = M0 ⊂ M1 ⊂ ... ⊂ Mn = M with Mi+1/Mi ≅ A/pi for primes pi, so Ass M is finite (Exercise 6.6.J and 6.6.K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build filtration inductively using Proposition 6.6.10; every associated prime appears among the pi, though some pi may be non-associated (Exercise 6.6.L).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal primes are associated
rubrics_metrics.description: If p corresponds to an irreducible component of Supp M (a minimal prime over Supp M) then [p] ∈ Ass M (Exercise 6.6.M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives that irreducible components' generic points appear among associated points for finitely generated modules over Noetherian rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of minimal primes are zerodivisors (Noetherian and non-Noetherian remark)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian then any element of a minimal prime p is a zerodivisor; this holds without Noetherian hypotheses by localization argument (Remark 6.6.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that pA_p is unique prime in A_p so elements become nilpotent in A_p and hence zerodivisors globally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support equals associated points for finitely generated modules (Noetherian)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated over a Noetherian ring A then Supp M = Ass M (Proposition 6.6.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines previous inclusions and existence/finiteness results; important consolidation of the theory in Noetherian setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ass commutes with localization
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M be a finitely-generated module over Noetherian A and S a multiplicative set; then Ass_{S^{-1}A}(S^{-1}M) = {S^{-1}p : p ∈ Ass_A(M), p ∩ S = ∅} (Proposition 6.6.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs injections and uses support commuting with localization; Exercise 6.6.Q covers support-commutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of embedded primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Associated primes that are not the generic points of irreducible components of Supp M are called embedded primes (6.6.27–6.6.28).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric picture: embedded points are non-generic associated points, e.g., correspond to 'embedded' structure supported at lower-dimensional loci; hypersurfaces in A^n_k have no embedded points (Exercise 6.6.F / remark).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedded primes imply nonreduced localizations
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is an embedded prime of a ring A then A_p is nonreduced (Exercise 6.6.S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties embedded primes to local nonreducedness; conversely reduced rings have no embedded primes (Exercise 6.6.R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme-theoretic density characterized by associated points
rubrics_metrics.description: An open subscheme U of a locally Noetherian scheme X is scheme-theoretically dense iff U contains all the associated points of X (6.6.33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheme-theoretic density is stronger than topological density; uses injectivity of restriction map Γ(X, OX) -> Γ(U, OX|_U) when U contains Ass X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational functions defined via associated points
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational function on a locally Noetherian scheme is an element of the image of Γ(U, O_U) in the total ring of fractions for some open U containing all associated points; equivalently colimit over opens containing Ass X (6.6.36, 6.6.Z).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rational functions have maximal domain of definition; regularity at a point means point lies in that maximal domain. Complement is the indeterminacy locus. Example on Spec k[x,y]/(y^2,xy) given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated points of integral schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: For integral schemes the only associated point is the generic point, so the above notion of rational functions recovers the usual function field K(X) (6.6.37).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to check compatibility with earlier definitions for integral schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary ideals and associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal I is p-primary iff √I = p (and equivalently A/I has only one associated prime p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary decomposition (for Noetherian rings) has associated primes equal to radicals of components; historical note (6.6.38).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence notions and closure properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and implications: coherent ⇒ finitely presented ⇒ finitely generated; coherent modules form an abelian category and are closed under kernels, cokernels, finite direct sums, images of maps from finitely generated modules, etc. (Section 6.7 and exercises 6.7.A–6.7.L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series of exercises establish stability of coherence under exact sequences, direct sums, Hom with finitely presented domain, tensor with finitely presented domain, and that a finite direct sum of coherent modules is coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of ringed spaces: definition and local description
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of ringed spaces π : X -> Y is a continuous map of underlying spaces together with a map of sheaves O_Y -> π_* O_X (equivalently π^{-1} O_Y -> O_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivation: pullback of functions and values; for affine schemes a ring map B -> A induces Spec A -> Spec B (Exercise 7.2.F). Composition, open embeddings, and gluing of morphisms are discussed (7.2.1 and exercises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward and pullback of O-modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a morphism of ringed spaces π : X -> Y, pushforward π_* gives a functor Mod O_X -> Mod O_Y (Exercise 7.2.C), and there is a pullback (tensoring π^{-1} with O_X) producing π^* : Mod O_Y -> Mod O_X, left adjoint to π_* (Exercise 7.2.D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises detail functoriality, adjointness, compatibility with composition, and the push-pull map in diagrams of ringed spaces.
